newsitem.title: USA: U.S. FDA moves against some Centeon products.
newsitem.headline: U.S. FDA moves against some Centeon products.

text.p: U.S. drug regulators announced on Tuesday a limit to the distribution of some products of Centeon LLC, a joint venture between Rhone-Poulenc Rorer Inc and Hoechst AG, because of faulty manufacturing standards.

The Food and Drug Administration said the limit, agreed in a consent decree between the FDA, the Justice Department and Centeon, would continue until Centeon's manufacturing standards met the FDA's safety and quality requirements.
It exempted two products made by Centeon -- H.P. Acthar Gel, used to treat infant seizures, and MVI-12, an injectable multivitamin.
The FDA said it believed the continued availability of the two products was essential for the public health.
It said Centeon would not be allowed to distribute any of its other products in interstate commerce until it could show that its manufacturing process met FDA standards.

Among the shortcomings of the Centeon plant at Bradley, Ill., were a lack of personnel to assure the plant is clean, that quality controls are maintained and that records are kept to monitor accurately the production process.

The FDA noted that Centeon last September recalled a lot of human albumin because it was contaminated with bacterial agents associated with septicemia, a blood infection that can be life-threatening, and that other lots were recalled later.
